Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we have a shared record and a set of concrete next steps.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Production latency spikes during morning and evening batch windows; observed p95 jumps from ~160ms to ~420ms under concurrent traffic.
- Cold-start variability when models are scaled up causes increased tail latency (KV cache misses noted).
- Target constraints: p95 <= 200ms for user-visible responses; sustained throughput ~350–500 rps with 2:1 peak bursts; aim for 99.9% availability.
- Security/regulatory: data must stay inside VPC, audit logs retained 13 months, and KMS integration required.

Model details you shared (confirming)
- Internal model: LLaMA-derivative, ~70B parameters, ~8k context, uses top-k sampling in prod.
- Primary workload: short prompts (~40–100 tokens) for classification + longer generation on-demand.

Immediate asks we agreed on
1) You will send a representative 48h traffic trace + a few sample prompt/response pairs (attachment preferred) — we can use this to size batches and caching.
2) We’ll run an initial topology recommendation and performance estimate (cost + expected p95/p99) and come back with a mutual action plan.
3) Technical deep-dive with Markus (engine) to align on quantization + caching approach — proposed window Thu/Fri next week.

Attachments: please upload the 48h trace (PDF/CSV) and the example prompt set. I attached a draft mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx) for your team to edit.

Proposed next steps (simple)

Subject: Fwd: Novaflow — inference topology, SLOs & next steps (technical readout)

Forwarding a short technical readout ahead of our deep-dive. I reviewed the trace and the sample prompts — summarized recommendations below.

Summary of constraints
- Model: ~70B, 8k context. Mixed workload: 80% short-response classification (<=100 tokens), 20% long gen.
- Traffic profile: sustained baseline ~320 rps with 2x–3x peaks for 10–20 minutes. Bursty concurrently across regions.

Topology recommendation
1) Primary: Redwood Dedicated GPU pool (A100 80GB equivalence) inside customer VPC with private control plane. Use multiple shards per model for throughput; target 4 shards for 70B to hit baseline throughput.
2) Multi-variant routing: run a quantized 13B variant (int4 GPTQ) as a low-latency fast path for short prompts; route by latency budget and confidence. Fallback to 70B for complex queries.
3) Fallback policy: when Dedicated pool is saturated, route to Redwood Hosted fast-slot instances (lower-cost preemptible pool) with strict request-quotas and trimmed context to preserve latency.

Performance controls and SLO mapping
- Batching: fixed per-GPU micro-batching with dynamic batch cap; aim for avg batching latency <= 25–30ms; max batch size tuned to keep p95 token latency budget.
- Caching: aggressive prefix + KV cache for repeated prompts; use 12h TTL for session-level caches and active pre-warming on deploy/scale events.
- SLOs (target): p50 token latency ~40ms, p95 token latency <= 180ms for short paths, p99 token latency <= 400ms under steady-state; end-to-end request p95 <= 200ms target for short prompts.
- Throughput: design for sustained 400 rps with headroom to 1,000 rps burst via autoscaling + hosted fallback.

Quantization & model variants
- Recommend GPTQ-style int4 for 13B fast path; evaluate QAT int4 for 70B if accuracy drop is unacceptable. Expect 2–3x memory reduction with int4.
- KV-cache memory planning: with 8k context, per-shard KV can be large; reserve extra GPU memory headroom or use remote KV-store for very large sessions.

Observability & validation
- Perf harness: run replay of the 48h trace in our staging fleet (we’ll provide instructions) to produce expected p95/p99 and cost estimates.
- Regression tests: run quality evals on sample prompt set after quantization to check delta.

Actionable asks from Novaflow before the deep-dive
- Confirm whether the 13B trimmed variant is acceptable as a quality-latency tradeoff for mobile clients.
- Share a sample of model binaries (or model spec + tokenizer details) so we can validate memory and tokenization overhead.
- Confirm regulatory constraints for egress and KMS key rotation window.

I’ll bring a sizing estimate to the Thu 16:00 PT call. If you want I can draft two cost scenarios (Dedicated-heavy vs Hybrid fallback) prior to the meeting.
